CFB Kingston.question: Located north of King's _____ 2, the name of the military base and village was in honour of the Royal Navy's Rear-Admiral Sir Robert Barrie who served during the War of 1812
CFB Kingston.fact: Located north of King's Highway 2, the name of the military base and village was in honour of the Royal Navy's Rear-Admiral Sir Robert Barrie who served during the War of 1812. In 1937 the base expanded to the south side of King's Highway 2 with the opening of the Vimy Barracks, named in honour of the Battle of Vimy Ridge.

CFB Kingston.question: From 1945 to 1969 the Mc_____ were host to the Royal Canadian Electrical and Mechanical Engineers School
CFB Kingston.fact: Following the war, the original part of Barriefield Military Camp on the north side of the King's Highway 2 was renamed the McNaughton Barracks in honour of the Canadian Army's General A.G.L. McNaughton who served during the First and Second World Wars. From 1945 to 1969 the McNaughton Barracks were host to the Royal Canadian Electrical and Mechanical Engineers School.

CFB Kingston.question: In September 1975, _____ was disbanded and the base was transferred to Canadian Forces Training System
CFB Kingston.fact: CFB Kingston was placed under Training Command and was responsible for providing training facilities and support services to its integral units and lodger units. In September 1975, Training Command was disbanded and the base was transferred to Canadian Forces Training System.

CFB Kingston.question: Mc_____ earned 2011 PGA Tour playing privileges in December, 2010
CFB Kingston.fact: Matt McQuillan, now a member of the Canadian Professional Golf Tour and a tour winner, learned the game at Garrison as a junior player in the 1990s. McQuillan earned 2011 PGA Tour playing privileges in December, 2010.
